scenes.title: SMTC Campus Membrane Test Aisle
scenes.institution: Nanyang Technological University — Singapore Membrane Technology Centre
scenes.reference_notes: Inspected brochure page 3 shows six captioned views: analytical benches, industrial research aisle, membrane fabrication machines, pressure-retarded-osmosis apparatus and separate outdoor pilot facilities. These are multiple sites/zones, not one room. This is a selected reference-informed room subset; exact dimensions, topology and OEM geometry are not verified.
observed_cues: The official brochure separates an analytical room, campus industrial project area, membrane fabrication equipment and the outdoor Tuas pilot site.
The campus industrial area photograph shows open metal frames on both sides of a working aisle, pipes, computer terminals and suspended services.
Brochure device photograph shows membrane modules, white-ended components, fittings and black tubing.

equipment.role: Campus research membrane frame with isolation valve and water-vial carriage

support.evidence: Integral authored feet/frame contacts floor; spatial dimensions estimated from references

task.name: Position a water-vial carrier and inspect valve travel
task.description: Actuate the visible sampling carriage and isolation-valve handle on a representative membrane research skid.
task.observable: Valve angle and sample-carriage displacement; no filtration measurement.

layout_rationale: Reconstruct the campus industrial-project aisle only, with paired framed test rigs, a separate preparation enclosure and overhead service carriers.
Open steel chassis, grounded feet, membrane module housings, fittings, gauges and a three-vial carriage distinguish this room from a generic chemistry laboratory.
Source does not prove the exact neighbouring machines or measured room dimensions; casting enclosure and rig routing are representative. Tuas outdoor container and pilot bank are excluded.
A central 3 m aisle links entry and rig work zones; the sample carriage moves towards open operator space.

scenes.title: Moreton Bay Research Aquarium
scenes.institution: The University of Queensland — Moreton Bay Research Station
scenes.reference_notes: Opened the facility page and visually inspected its aquarium photograph: a wet room with large circular tanks, yellow aquarium racks, plumbing and ceiling services. The text distinguishes the aquarium from four other laboratories. This is a selected reference-informed room subset; exact dimensions, topology and OEM geometry are not verified.
observed_cues: The official wet-lab photograph shows large circular tanks, yellow rack structures, overhead services and wet-room plumbing.
The official facility description lists two 4000 L tanks, one 10000 L tank and three racks each fitting twelve standard tanks.
The aquarium is a dedicated wet laboratory separate from the station's four other laboratory rooms.

equipment.role: Authored instrumented probe bridge over a reference-informed round tank

support.evidence: Integral authored feet/frame contacts floor; spatial dimensions estimated from references

task.name: Position an inert monitoring probe over a tank
task.description: Traverse and lower a visible probe on a grounded bridge. The bridge is an authored task fixture, not verified UQ equipment.
task.observable: Probe traverse and immersion position; static water and no calibrated measurement.

layout_rationale: Three large circular tanks and three yellow racks with twelve tank positions each establish the documented aquarium scale and characteristic arrangement.
Overhead feeds, return/sump context, water surfaces and a grated floor drain produce a distinct wet-room environment; the large-tank arrangement is estimated.
A motorized sampling bridge is added as an original mechanical-control fixture; it was not visible in the reference photograph and is not claimed as UQ hardware.
Only broad spatial cues can be recovered from the small published photograph; modeled tank geometry estimates nominal capacity classes without certifying fluid volume.
The left entry opens into the clear zone between the round tanks and rear rack wall; no desks or small tabletop-only aquarium substitute is used.
limitations: Room dimensions and unseen placements are estimated from public images; no institution has validated this scene.
Original procedural geometry, no downloaded OEM CAD and no source photographs packaged as textures.
